event.description: An Evening with Cheryl Slay Carr Finding Home: Songs of Love and Justice A Benefit Concert Supporting I Am Next Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Doors Open: 6:15 PM Concert: 7:00 PM Location: National Museum of African American Music | 510 Broadway, Nashville, TN 37203 Join us for Finding Home: Songs of Love and Justice, a powerful evening of music, storytelling, and community led by acclaimed vocalist Cheryl Slay Carr and featured guest artist — MarQo “Q” Patton. Finding Home explores the many meanings of “home”— from love and identity to resilience, faith, justice, and belonging. Each song becomes part of a larger musical journey, inviting audiences to reflect on the places, people, and experiences that shape who we are and where we find a sense of home. Presented as a benefit performance supporting I Am Next, Finding Home is more than a concert—it is an evening rooted in the power of music to connect us, inspire us, and move us toward a more just and compassionate future. Come find your way home. About I Am Next: I Am Next supports youth aging out of foster care by empowering youth with the resources, relationships and much-needed time to find their footing and build lasting stability. event.venue_json: {"id":4699,"global_id":"www.nmaam.org?id=4699","venue":"National Museum of African American Music","address":"510 Broadway","city":"Nashville","country":"United States","state":"TN","zip":"37203","website":"https://www.nmaam.org","phone":"6153018724","url":"https://www.nmaam.org/venue/national-museum-of-african-american-music/","show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description: The National Museum of African American Music Presents In The Pocket A Celebration with Lee Garrett Saturday, October 17, 2026 | 2:00 PM – 4:00 PM Amplify Lounge | National Museum of African American Music Join the National Museum of African American Music for a special edition of In The Pocket, celebrating the life, music, and legacy of Grammy-nominated songwriter, artist, and radio pioneer Lee Garrett. Garrett’s career is woven into the fabric of American music. With songwriting credits including ‘Signed, Sealed, Delivered I’m Yours’ (co-written with Stevie Wonder), The Spinners’ ‘It’s a Shame’ and Jermaine Jackson’s ‘Let’s Get Serious,’ ‘Better Than Walking Out’ by Marlena Shaw and ‘Heart Be Still’ for Frankie Valli. He made history as the first blind Top 40 radio DJ, and this year marks the 50th anniversary of his original Heat for the Feets, featuring UK hit ‘You’re My Everything’. Moderated by Grammy Award-winning musician and producer Shannon Sanders, this intimate conversation will take audiences behind the songs and defining moments of Lee Garrett’s journey — where he’ll share stories from his career, reflect on his friendships and creative relationships, and explore the impact their generation of artists and songwriters have had on music and culture. event.description: Memphis’ emerging sound joins forces with Nashville’s, and NMAAM is capturing this unforgettable story on an unforgettable night. The National Museum of African American Music and TappedIN 901 proudly present First Note: For the Love of R&B, a groundbreaking show created to magnify the musical connection between Memphis and Nashville, TN. Born from a simple but radical belief: emerging artists deserve more than a stage. They deserve a platform. Beginning October 24, NMAAM will become the epicenter of something new—a conduit bridging the soulful sound of Memphis with the harmony of Music City. Artists who are just writing their first chapters will share space with fans who feel it, industry executives who need to hear it, and a community of museum visitors who will carry those sounds far beyond these walls. Memphis and Nashville share a story, and NMAAM is the home where the next chapter begins. Register Here
